title: Orphan-rewire sweep policy: always re-check, never mark-independent
summary: For the periodic note-orphan rewire sweep: do NOT add a permanent 'independent' flag to skip zero-edge notes on future sweeps. Re-check them every sweep instead. Rationale: (1) independence is not durable — the graph grows, so a note with no neighbor >=0.25 today gets a legitimate match when a related node is created later; a permanent flag would lock it out of links it should receive. (2) Re-checking a true orphan is side-effect-free: scoreMatches is a read and addEdge only writes when something clears threshold, so no match => no write => no churn. (3) A flag is state that must be invalidated whenever any node is added, which negates its benefit. If rescan cost is ever measured to matter at scale, the correct optimization is a graph-epoch watermark (stamp each orphan with a counter that bumps on node insert; skip orphans whose stamp == current epoch; a new node re-eligibles all orphans), NOT a permanent flag. Build the plain re-check now; add the watermark only if measured.
